chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man bought the hay of a stack, each kurra for a known amount. He takes possession of the hay and sells it before the grain is measured. He (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.بَيْدَرٍ: A stack or heap of hay/grain.
key_terms.تِبْنَ: Hay or straw, specifically used as animal feed.
key_terms.كُرٍّ: A unit of measurement (volume or weight) used in trade.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it; it is permissible.
key_terms.يَقْبِضُ: To take possession or seize (in a legal trade context).
key_terms.يُكَالَ: To be measured (specifically by volume using a container).

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell hay before measuring the grain in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of selling hay from a stack (*baydar*) by weight or count (*kurra*) for a fixed price, even if the buyer resells it before the accompanying grain is fully measured. This ruling highlights the flexibility in commercial transactions within Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the validity of the initial contract and the timing of final measurement, thereby facilitating trade efficiency while maintaining contractual integrity.
